subproblem.title: Compactly supported finite-mass IM filling of an IM boundary for d < P, using the in-range isoperimetric filling (parent step 3, V3)
subproblem.statement: Assume (MR), (IMC)(c), (VO) and (Isor). (MR) is the frozen type of the accepted cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure: M_W(X) = R.measure(W) whenever the IMRep R represents X ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, W open. (IMC)(c): for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and IM A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), A − B is IM. (VO) is the frozen type of the accepted dtc_vanish_off_support: S(ω) = 0 for every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S. (Isor) is the in-range isoperimetric filling, verbatim the corresponding hypothesis of the selected node (the second conjunct of the frozen type of dtc_bc_tc_cl_deformation_isoperimetric): for all P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P there is a real c ≥ 1 such that every IM Z ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, ∂Z = 0 and M(Z) < ∞ equals ∂Y for an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with M(Y) ≤ c(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}M(Z) and spt Y ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt Z) < 3√P(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}}. Let P, d ∈ ℕ with d < P, and let T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) have compact support, with M(∂T) < ∞ and ∂T IM. Then there is an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = ∂T, M(Y) < ∞ and spt Y compact. Notation: SimonGMT currents in U = ℝ^P, M = mass = M_{ℝ^P}, spt = GeometricCurrentOn.support, IM = IsIntegerMultiplicity. This is the unaccepted dmcbr_cc_compact_im_filling / cbr_cc_compact_im_filling with the isoperimetric hypothesis restricted to the range m + 1 < P.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → (∀ (P m : ℕ), m + 1 < P → ∃ c : ℝ, 1 ≤ c ∧ ∀ Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Z → IsCompact Z.support → Z.boundary = 0 → Z.mass < ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ Y.boundary = Z ∧ Y.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * (2 * c * Z.mass.toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (m + 1)) * Z.mass.toReal) ∧ Y.support ⊆ thickening (3 * Real.sqrt P * (2 * c * Z.mass.toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (m + 1))) Z.support) → ∀ (P d : ℕ), d < P → ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)), IsCompact T.support → T.boundary.mass < ∞ → IsIntegerMultiplicity T.boundary → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ Y.boundary = T.boundary ∧ Y.mass < ∞ ∧ IsCompact Y.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the supplied proof (parent V3), and Simon Ch. 6, proof of 8.2 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 2322–2337: "the general case of the theorem follows from the special case when ∂T = 0"). It is stated for one current T with compact support and IM boundary of finite mass. For n = d + 1 ≥ 2 it uses (Isor) with m := d − 1, which is in range because m + 1 = d < P. For n = 1 it is the segment construction. Deviation from the supplied proof: the base point is 0 instead of a point x₀ ∉ {x_i}; a point x = 0 then contributes the zero segment current, which segment_current allows (a = b). Siblings used: support_vanish (rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish), current_algebra (cbr_cc_current_algebra) part (c), segment_current (dmcbr_cc_segment_current) and zero_current_sum (dmcbr_cc_zero_current_finite_sum). Notation: M := M_{ℝ^P}; for a 0-form g, g(x)⟨⟩ is the value of the 0-covector g(x) on the empty tuple; dη := exteriorDerivativeTestOn ℝ^P applied to η, so ∂S(η) = S(dη).
1. spt ∂T ⊆ spt T, and spt ∂T is compact. Let η be a test d-form whose tsupport is disjoint from spt T. Since tsupport dη ⊆ tsupport η (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), tsupport dη is disjoint from spt T too. So ∂T(η) = T(dη) = 0 by (VO). Apply support_vanish with U := ℝ^P (open), K := spt T (compact) and F := ∂T. It gives spt ∂T ⊆ spt T, and spt ∂T is compact.
Case d = m + 1 (n ≥ 2).
2. Filling of the cycle. Z := ∂T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) is IM, has compact support (step 1) and finite mass, and ∂Z = ∂∂T = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary). Since m + 1 = d < P, (Isor) with (P, m) gives a constant c ≥ 1. Its conclusion for Z gives an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) = 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = Z = ∂T, M(Y) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(c(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}M(Z)) < ∞ and spt Y ⊆ thickening_r(spt Z), where r := 3√P(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}.
3. spt Y is compact. spt Z is compact, hence bounded. So its r-thickening is bounded (Bornology.IsBounded.thickening), and its closure C is compact, because ℝ^P is proper. Let ω be a test form whose tsupport is disjoint from C. Then it is disjoint from spt Y ⊆ thickening_r(spt Z) ⊆ C, so Y(ω) = 0 by (VO). Applying support_vanish with K := C shows that spt Y is compact. So Y is as required.
Case d = 0 (n = 1).
4. Point-mass form. ∂T ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P) is IM with compact support (step 1). zero_current_sum (with (MR) and (VO)) gives a finite set F ⊆ spt ∂T ⊆ spt T and integers m(x) with ∂T(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)·g(x)⟨⟩ for every test 0-form g.
5. Total multiplicity zero. spt T is compact, so spt T ⊆ B_ρ(0) for some ρ > 0. Let ψ be a smooth bump function with ψ = 1 on B̄_ρ(0) and support in B_{2ρ}(0) (ContDiffBump with radii ρ < 2ρ). Let g be the test 0-form g(y) := constOfIsEmpty(ψ(y)), so g(y)⟨⟩ = ψ(y). It is smooth and compactly supported.
 For y ∈ B_ρ(0), ψ = 1 on a neighbourhood of y, so Dψ(y) = 0 and dg(y) = 0 (extDeriv_constOfIsEmpty). Hence tsupport dg lies in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ B_ρ(0), which contains {dg ≠ 0} and is disjoint from spt T ⊆ B_ρ(0). So ∂T(g) = T(dg) = 0 by (VO).
 On the other hand, F ⊆ spt T ⊆ B_ρ(0), where ψ = 1, so ∂T(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)ψ(x) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x). Therefore Σ_{x∈F} m(x) = 0.
6. Segments. For each x ∈ ℝ^P, segment_current (with (MR), a := 0, b := x) gives an IM S_x ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) with ∂S_x(g) = g(x)⟨⟩ − g(0)⟨⟩ for every test 0-form g, M(S_x) < ∞ and spt S_x ⊆ [0, x].
7. The filling. Apply current_algebra (c) with (IMC)(c), U := ℝ^P, ι := ℝ^P, the finite set F, the currents S_x and the integers m(x). It gives an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) with Y(ω) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)S_x(ω) for every ω, and M_W(Y) ≤ Σ_{x∈F} |m(x)|M_W(S_x) for every W.
8. ∂Y = ∂T. For a test 0-form η, using steps 6, 5 and 4:
 ∂Y(η) = Y(dη) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)S_x(dη) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)(η(x)⟨⟩ − η(0)⟨⟩) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)η(x)⟨⟩ − (Σ_{x∈F} m(x))η(0)⟨⟩ = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)η(x)⟨⟩ = ∂T(η).
 So ∂Y = ∂T (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
9. Finite mass. M(Y) ≤ Σ_{x∈F}|m(x)|M(S_x) < ∞, a finite sum of finite terms.
10. spt Y is compact. C := ⋃_{x∈F}[0, x] is compact: it is a finite union of segments, each the image of [0, 1] under the continuous map s ↦ s·x. Let ω be a test form whose tsupport is disjoint from C. For each x ∈ F, tsupport ω is then disjoint from spt S_x ⊆ [0, x], so S_x(ω) = 0 by (VO); hence Y(ω) = 0. Applying support_vanish with K := C shows that spt Y is compact. ∎

This tactic proof of exactly the frozen statement compiled with lake env lean after import GMT.Ch07.Submission inside namespace GMT.Ch07 with the contract's opens, with the sibling declarations Submission.cbr_cc_current_algebra, Submission.rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish, Submission.dmcbr_cc_segment_current, Submission.dmcbr_cc_zero_current_finite_sum available at their frozen types; #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound and those sibling declarations.
  intro hMR hIMC hVO hISO P d hdP T hTc hbm hbim
  -- Step 1: `spt ∂T ⊆ spt T`, and `spt ∂T` is compact
  obtain ⟨hbsub, hbc⟩ := Submission.rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish P d univ T.support
    T.boundary isOpen_univ hTc (subset_univ _) fun η hη => by
      rw [GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply]
      exact hVO P (d + 1) univ T (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ d η) (Disjoint.mono_left
        (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d)) hη)
  rcases d with _ | m
  · -- Case `d = 0`.  Step 4: `∂T = Σ_{x ∈ F} m(x) δ_x`
    obtain ⟨F, m, hF, hsum⟩ :=
      Submission.dmcbr_cc_zero_current_finite_sum hMR hVO P T.boundary hbim hbc
    have hFT : ∀ x ∈ F, x ∈ T.support := fun x hx => hbsub (hF hx)
    -- Step 5: `Σ_{x ∈ F} m(x) = 0`, testing `∂T` on a bump `0`-form `≡ 1` near `spt T`
    obtain ⟨ρ, hρ, hTρ⟩ := hTc.isBounded.subset_ball_lt 0 (0 : Euclid P)
    let ψ : ContDiffBump (0 : Euclid P) := ⟨ρ, 2 * ρ, hρ, by linarith⟩
    let gf : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0 := fun y =>
      ContinuousAlternatingMap.constOfIsEmpty ℝ (Euclid P) (Fin 0) (ψ y)
    have hg : IsTestForm gf ∧ tsupport gf ⊆ univ :=
      ⟨⟨(ContinuousAlternatingMap.constOfIsEmptyLIE ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ (Fin 0)).contDiff.comp
          ψ.contDiff,
        ψ.hasCompactSupport.comp_left
          (map_zero (ContinuousAlternatingMap.constOfIsEmptyLIE ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ (Fin 0)))⟩,
        subset_univ _⟩
    let g : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 0 := ⟨gf, hg⟩
    have hdg : ∀ y ∈ ball (0 : Euclid P) ρ, exteriorDerivative gf y = 0 := by
      intro y hy
      have hψ : fderiv ℝ ψ y = 0 :=
        (ψ.eventuallyEq_one_of_mem_ball hy).fderiv_eq.trans (fderiv_const_apply 1)
      show extDeriv (fun x => ContinuousAlternatingMap.constOfIsEmpty ℝ (Euclid P) (Fin 0) (ψ x))
        y = 0
      rw [extDeriv_constOfIsEmpty, hψ]
      ext v
      simp
    have hTg : T.boundary g = 0 := by
      rw [GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply]
      refine hVO P (0 + 1) univ T (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ 0 g)
        (Disjoint.mono ?_ hTρ disjoint_compl_left)
      exact closure_minimal (fun y hy hyρ => hy (hdg y hyρ)) isOpen_ball.isClosed_compl
    have htot : ∑ x ∈ F, (m x : ℝ) = 0 := by
      refine Eq.trans (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x hx => ?_) ((hsum g).symm.trans hTg)
      show (m x : ℝ) = (m x : ℝ) * ψ x
      rw [ψ.one_of_mem_closedBall (ball_subset_closedBall (hTρ (hFT x hx))), mul_one]
    -- Step 6: segments `S_x` with `∂S_x = δ_x − δ_0` and `spt S_x ⊆ [0, x]`
    choose S hSim hSb hSm hSsupp using Submission.dmcbr_cc_segment_current hMR P (0 : Euclid P)
    -- Step 7: `Y = Σ_{x ∈ F} m(x) S_x` is integer multiplicity
    obtain ⟨Y, hYim, hYeval, hYmass⟩ :=
      Submission.cbr_cc_current_algebra.2.2 hIMC P 1 univ (Euclid P) F S m isOpen_univ
        fun x _ => hSim x
    refine ⟨Y, hYim, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · -- Step 8: `∂Y = ∂T`
      ext η
      calc Y.boundary η
          = ∑ x ∈ F, (m x : ℝ) * S x (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ 0 η) := by
            rw [GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply]
            exact hYeval (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ 0 η)
        _ = ∑ x ∈ F, ((m x : ℝ) * (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) x (fun i => i.elim0) -
              (m x : ℝ) * (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) 0 (fun i => i.elim0)) :=
            Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => by
              rw [← mul_sub, ← hSb x η, GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply]
        _ = ∑ x ∈ F, (m x : ℝ) * (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) x (fun i => i.elim0) -
              (∑ x ∈ F, (m x : ℝ)) * (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) 0 (fun i => i.elim0) := by
            rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_mul]
        _ = T.boundary η := by rw [htot, zero_mul, sub_zero, hsum η]
    · -- Step 9: `M(Y) ≤ Σ_{x ∈ F} |m(x)| M(S_x) < ∞`
      exact (hYmass univ).trans_lt (ENNReal.sum_lt_top.2 fun x _ =>
        ENNReal.mul_lt_top (ENNReal.natCast_lt_top _) (hSm x))
    · -- Step 10: `Y` vanishes off the compact `⋃_{x ∈ F} [0, x]`
      have hC : IsCompact (⋃ x ∈ F, segment ℝ (0 : Euclid P) x) :=
        F.isCompact_biUnion fun x _ => by
          rw [segment_eq_image_lineMap]
          exact isCompact_Icc.image AffineMap.lineMap_continuous
      refine (Submission.rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish P 1 univ _ Y isOpen_univ hC
        (subset_univ _) fun ω hω => ?_).2
      rw [hYeval ω]
      refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun x hx => ?_
      rw [hVO P 1 univ (S x) ω (hω.mono_right ((hSsupp x).trans
        (subset_iUnion₂ (s := fun x (_ : x ∈ F) => segment ℝ (0 : Euclid P) x) x hx))), mul_zero]
  · -- Case `d = m + 1`.  Step 2: fill the cycle `Z = ∂T` by (Isor) with `m + 1 < P`
    obtain ⟨c, -, hfill⟩ := hISO P m hdP
    obtain ⟨Y, hYim, hYb, hYm, hYsupp⟩ :=

    refine ⟨Y, hYim, hYb, hYm.trans_lt ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top, ?_⟩
    -- Step 3: `Y` vanishes off the compact closure of a bounded thickening of `spt Z`
    exact (Submission.rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish P (m + 2) univ _ Y isOpen_univ

proof_key_steps: spt ∂T ⊆ spt T is compact ((VO) for T, tsupport dη ⊆ tsupport η, support_vanish).
d = m + 1: (Isor) with m + 1 = d < P fills the cycle ∂T by an IM Y inside a bounded thickening of spt ∂T, so M(Y) < ∞ and spt Y is compact (support_vanish).
d = 0: ∂T = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)δ_x (zero_current_sum), and Σ m(x) = 0 by testing ∂T on a bump 0-form ≡ 1 near spt T and using (VO).
Y := Σ m(x)[[0, x]] (segment_current, current_algebra (c)) is IM with ∂Y = ∂T, M(Y) < ∞ and spt Y ⊆ ⋃[0, x] compact.

subproblem.title: Integer slice property of IM currents with IM boundary in ℝ^P from BR_P(d) in the single dimension P (parent step 5, V4(i))
subproblem.statement: Assume (IMC), (SL), (MM) and (RU). (IMC) is the frozen type of the accepted cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub: (a) a.e. locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested Borel sets; (b) for every IMRep R in an open U and every Borel E there are a current A and an IMRep R' representing A with carrier R.carrier ∩ E, multiplicity R.mult and orientation R.orient; (c) for open U, differences of IM currents in 𝒟_n(U) are IM; (d) IMRep orientations satisfy |orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ⌞carrier-a.e. x and all α. (SL) is the frozen type of the accepted cmc_slice_mass_bounds: for open U, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) represented by (μ, ξ) and ∂T by (μ', ξ') (measures finite on compact subsets of U, a.e. strongly measurable fields, a.e. bounded by 1 in the coefficient norm) and L-Lipschitz f, there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) for open W, and ∫_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t) dt ≤ L·μ(W ∩ {a<f<b}). (MM) is the measurable slice-mass majorant, verbatim the (MM) conjunct of the frozen type of dtc_bc_tc_cl_foundations (the selected node's prerequisite foundations): for measures μ_j on ℝ^P, continuous f, G ⊆ ℝ^P, a, b ∈ ℝ, L ≥ 0 and Z_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] with μ_j(G ∩ {a<f<b}) < ∞ and Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t−h<f<t}) for t ∈ (a, b), there is a measurable g with liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g ≤ L·liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a<f<b}). (RU) is the frozen type of the accepted cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq: if, in an open U, three admissible pairs (μ_i, ξ_i) satisfy ∫ξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫ξ₃(ω)dμ₃ for every test form ω, then the same identity holds for the integrals over every Borel set B. Let P, d ∈ ℕ and assume BR_P(d): for every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and every IM R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, ∂R is IM. Then every IM X ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) whose boundary ∂X is IM has the integer slice property (ISP): for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of X and (μ', ξ') of ∂X in ℝ^P (Borel measures finite on every compact set; a.e. strongly measurable (d+1)- resp. d-vector fields with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ'-a.e. x; X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ and ∂X(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms) and every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, every pair A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms has ∂A − B IM. ISP is the predicate written out verbatim in the frozen types of the selected node's prerequisites slice_limit, lower_density and cycle_im (dtc_bc_tc_cl_slice_property_of_weak_limit, dtc_bc_tc_cl_lower_density, dtc_bc_tc_cl_cycle_isIntegerMultiplicity). Notation: SimonGMT currents, M_W = massOn W, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α, Hⁿ = μHE[n], IM = IsIntegerMultiplicity, W ⊂⊂ U = CompactlyContained. This is the accepted dmcbr_cc_slice_property_of_im with BR(d) required only in the single dimension P.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the supplied proof (parent V4(i)): "If X and ∂X are IM with finite masses then X has ISP: for admissible representations and f, (SL) gives slices Z_t with locally finite mass for a.e. t ((MM)); A_t = X⌞{f<t} is IM by (IMC)(b) and (RU), likewise B_t; ∂A_t = B_t + Z_t has locally finite mass, so it is IM by BR_P(d) in ℝ^P, and Z_t = ∂A_t − B_t is IM by (IMC)(c)." The finite-mass hypotheses of step 5 are not needed. This is the argument of the accepted dmcbr_cc_slice_property_of_im, which applies BR only with U := ℝ^P in the given dimension P; so BR_P(d) at the single dimension P suffices. Siblings used: restrict_im (cbr_ccisp_restrict_isIntegerMultiplicity), ae_mass_finite (cbr_ccisp_ae_massOn_lt_top), mass_le_measure (cmc_fcl_massOn_le_measure_inter) and current_algebra (cbr_cc_current_algebra), part (b). Notation: M_W(Z) := Z.massOn W; E_t := {x : f(x) < t}; ℝ^P is the open set U := univ; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.
1. Setup. Let X ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) be IM with ∂X IM. Let (μ, ξ) and (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of X and ∂X: μ(K), μ'(K) < ∞ for every compact K; ξ, ξ' are a.e. strongly measurable; |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ'-a.e. x (all covectors α); X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ and ∂X(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms. Let f be L-Lipschitz. Write (IMC) = (a) ∧ (b) ∧ (c) ∧ (d). Since f is continuous, every E_t is Borel (measurableSet_lt).
2. Slices. Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d, T := X, the pairs (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ'), f and L. Its hypotheses are exactly the admissibility conditions of step 1 (a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P has μ(K), μ'(K) < ∞). It gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) and B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{E_t}ξ(ω)dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{E_t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms. Moreover, with Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open W and every t.
3. Null set. Apply ae_mass_finite with (MM), P, q := d, U := ℝ^P, Z := (t ↦ Z_t), μ (finite on compact sets), the continuous f, L and the bound of step 2. It gives a Lebesgue-null set N ⊂ ℝ such that for every t ∉ N, M_W(Z_t) < ∞ for every bounded W ⊆ ℝ^P.
4. Reduction. Fix t ∉ N and currents A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{E_t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{E_t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms. Then A agrees with A_t and B with B_t on every test form, so A = A_t and B = B_t (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). It remains to show that Z_t = ∂A_t − B_t is IM.
5. A_t is IM. Apply restrict_im with (IMC)(b), (IMC)(d), (RU), P, q := d + 1, U := ℝ^P, the IM current X, A := A_t, (μ, ξ) and E := E_t. Its hypotheses hold: μ is finite on compact sets; ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable with the a.e. unit bound; X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ; E_t is Borel; and A_t(ω) = ∫_{E_t}ξ(ω)dμ.
6. B_t is IM. Apply restrict_im in the same way with q := d, the IM current ∂X, A := B_t, (μ', ξ') and E := E_t.
7. ∂A_t is IM. We apply BR_P(d) with U := ℝ^P and R := A_t, which is IM by step 5. Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P, i.e. closure W is compact.
 (i) W ⊆ closure W is bounded, so M_W(Z_t) < ∞ by step 3.
 (ii) Apply mass_le_measure with X := B_t, (μ', ξ'), E := E_t and V := W, using the a.e. unit bound of ξ' and the formula for B_t. It gives M_W(B_t) ≤ μ'(E_t ∩ W) ≤ μ'(closure W) < ∞, since closure W is compact.
 (iii) For every test d-form η, ∂A_t(η) = 1·Z_t(η) + 1·B_t(η), because Z_t(η) = ∂A_t(η) − B_t(η). So current_algebra (b) with p = q = 1 gives M_W(∂A_t) ≤ M_W(Z_t) + M_W(B_t) < ∞.
 Hence BR_P(d) shows that ∂A_t is IM.
8. Conclusion. ℝ^P is open and ∂A_t, B_t are IM by steps 7 and 6, so Z_t = ∂A_t − B_t is IM by (IMC)(c). By step 4, ∂A − B = Z_t is IM for every t ∉ N and every pair A, B with the slice formulas, i.e. for L¹-a.e. t. Since (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') and f were arbitrary, X has the integer slice property. ∎
